title: vault copy content differs from the ledger row's vault_sha256 -> NOT-VERIFIED(vault-hash-mismatch)
spec_case: V2: a vault file whose content differs from what the ledger's vault sha256 says (tamper case). Expected: NOT-VERIFIED with a reason mentioning hash mismatch.
path_convention: make-fixture.sh substitutes @FIXTURE_ROOT@ with the built root (absolute) and writes the substituted copy to <ROOT>/expected.json; this case-directory copy stays in placeholder form (pristine copy: expected.template.json) so it never points at a reaped temp root. Every path below is absolute after substitution.
ledger_header: source_path	source_sha256	vault_path	vault_sha256	exported_at	note

declared_ledger_rows.why: export-time bytes were byte-identical (row vault_sha256 = source bytes); the vault copy was edited after export, so its current digest is 91d9f779... (same byte count, different bytes) and the vault-side conjunct fails while the source side still matches
the vault copy differs from the export-time bytes by exactly one byte (a dropped trailing newline): current digest f1ebc6ec..., one byte shorter than the source
control row: both sides are byte-identical to the row's recorded digests, so a correct tool returns VERIFIED -- proving the tamper verdicts are not a blanket failure

expect.why: source path exists and its sha256 equals the row's source_sha256; the vault file exists but its sha256 (91d9f779...) differs from the row's vault_sha256 (59bea10a...) -- the vault-side conjunct is the only failure, and the files have identical byte counts

accept.note: per-target accept so harnesses that bind the case-level accept block to the primary target only still judge this row tolerantly; any reason containing 'mismatch' (or 'drift') satisfies the case

expect.why: same shape as the primary target but the vault copy differs by exactly one byte (dropped trailing newline): catches size- or mtime-based shortcuts and any non-byte-exact comparison
control: both paths exist and both digests equal the row's recorded values

accept.note: the primary target must be NOT-VERIFIED (r4 vocabulary) or NOT-SAFE (r2 baseline tool) and its first/primary reason or evidence must name a vault-side hash mismatch; any spelling containing 'vault' + ('hash' or 'sha' or 'digest') + 'mismatch' satisfies the case. A bare class token with the reason in a separate field also satisfies it as long as the reason names the vault side.

failure_modes_caught: vault-side skip: a tool that checks only the source hash reports VERIFIED -- caught by expect.verdict
source/vault confusion: a tool that compares the vault file against source_sha256, or the source file against vault_sha256, misclassifies the tamper as a source-side failure -- caught by must_not_be
class collapse: reporting SAFE or a generic NOT-SAFE with no vault-side reason instead of the distinct NOT-VERIFIED(vault-hash-mismatch) class -- caught by expect.verdict_string
blanket failure: a tool that never returns VERIFIED fails the matched control -- caught by expect[2].verdict
coarse tamper detection: a size/mtime shortcut passes the primary target (same byte count as source) but fails the subtle target (one byte shorter) -- caught by expect[1]

runner_notes.tool_cli: runners invoke the tool under test as: <tool> --ledger <file> --fallback <source-path>; the verdict is the first whitespace-separated token of the first output line starting with VERIFIED or NOT-VERIFIED
runner_notes.ledger_resolution: read the ledger path from this file's 'ledger' key (absolute after substitution); the case directory's ledger.tsv is a same-run copy
runner_notes.selftest: bash make-fixture.sh --selftest (fixture-integrity assertions A1-A8; exit 0 = fixture coherent)

git_context: the built root gets an offline `git init` (no commits) so repo-discovery code paths behave as on a real lane; no fetch/push/commit/branch/checkout/reset/rebase is ever run
